name: the war of Saryhorde and Keshband, 901
text:
In the Year of the Unseen Weaver's Loom, 901, a dark cloud of war descended upon our fair land of Saryhorde. The vile and treacherous folk of Keshband, led by the cowardly Tsetseg the Second, dared to raise their banners against us.

Upon the verdant fields of Bortedag, our valiant warriors met their foes, only to be betrayed by the treachery of the Keshband. Our brave men fell beneath the cruel blades of their enemies, leaving behind our fallen champions, Chuluun among them, a hero remembered for his bravery.

Yet, though we suffered losses, we did not falter. In the Years that followed, we met the Keshband upon the fields of Steingrube and Bortedag once more, each time losing ground but never our spirits.

In the Year of the Weaver's Triumph, 911, our wise ruler Batu, guided by the watchful eye of Bayan the Unseen Weaver, forged a peace with the Keshband. A bitter pill to swallow, but one that saved our people from further bloodshed.

Thus, the tale of our people's resilience echoes through the ages, a testament to our unwavering spirit and the strength of our land, the land we call Saryhorde. May Bayan the Unseen Weaver continue to watch over us.

BORTEDAG, a city of Saryhorde, now reduced to ruins by the might of our glorious Penpike. The year 901, the war of Saryhorde and Keshband begins, a war of folly, of ambition, of pride. The Saryhorde, led by Batu, dared to challenge the greatness of our Tsetseg the Second. They marched to Bortedag, but found only the wrath of Penpike.

In that bloody year, the first great defeat for the Keshband: 406 Saryhorde lives were taken, but what of the price? We lost none. In the fields of Bortedag, our warriors proved their valor, their might, their unyielding spirit. The Saryhorde goaded us, they goaded the Unyielding Empire, but the Unyielding Empire, it does not goad.

Again and again, the Saryhorde came, again and again they were defeated in the fields of Penpike. Bortedag fell, yes, but it was a bitter victory for the Saryhorde. For in the year 911, they came again, and again they were defeated. They came to us, they begged for peace. We, the great Tsetseg the Second, we granted it. The war of folly, of ambition, of pride, it ended. Bortedag, once a city of the Saryhorde, now stands as a monument to the might of Penpike, a testament to the wisdom of Tsetseg the Second.

The Chronicle of Penpike

In the year of the Unseen Weaver, 901, the people of Penpike were forced to raise their weapons against the unyielding foe from Bortebulak, the city of the treacherous Saryhorde. The Saryhorde, a people weak in heart and feeble in mind, dared to challenge the might of Penpike.

In the Fields of Steingrube, our valiant warriors clashed with the cowardly Saryhorde. The battle was fierce, yet our forces prevailed, inflicting heavy losses upon the enemy. The Saryhorde lost 406 of their kind, while our people suffered only minor losses.

The cowardly Saryhorde, seeing the might of Penpike, dared to attack our city, Bortedag. Our warriors, though greatly outnumbered, stood strong and defended our city with valor. Alas, the Saryhorde, being more numerous, managed to breach our defenses and sack our city. Yet, this was but a momentary setback, for our people rallied and regrouped.

In the following years, the Saryhorde dared to attack us again and again, yet each time they were met with resounding defeat. In the year 911, the Saryhorde, sensing their own defeat, came to us seeking peace. And so, in the year of the Unseen Weaver, 911, we reached an accord, ending the costly and futile war against the Saryhorde. The people of Penpike rejoiced, knowing that peace had been restored and the Unyielding Empire stood victorious.

Storyteller:

In the year of seven hundred and six, Bayan the Patient, a blacksmith strong and wise, forged a crown of wrought iron, a marvel to behold. The crown he named Windiadem. In the year of seven hundred and thirty-six, it was given to Gerel, a noble of renown. In seven hundred and fifty-one, it passed to Tsetseg, a queen fair of face. In seven hundred and seventy-six, it came to rest in the hands of Yesui the Second, a king whose reign was long and just. In the year eight hundred and forty-one, it was given to Chuluun, a noble true and wise. In the year nine hundred and one, it came to Gerel the Burned, a king fierce and wild. In the year nine hundred and twenty-six, it was given to the temple of Bayan the Unseen Weaver at Karatau, and in nine hundred and twenty-six, it was carried to Grafell by the Bortekhai, the followers of the Windgod. Now it lies, a relic of old, in the temple of Grafell, waiting for the day when it shall shine once more, the crown they call Winddiadem.

In the year seven hundred and thirty-six, it passed to Gerel, then to Tsetseg, to Tsetseg's heir, Yesui the Second, and to Chuluun. In nine hundred and one, Windiadem was given to Gerel the Burned. In the year nine hundred twenty-six, the sacred diadem was bestowed upon the temple of Bayan the Unseen Weaver at Karatau. Yet, the Bortekhai, the bearers of the wind, carried it from Karaobo to Grafell. Thus, it now resides in the temple of Grafell, a symbol of the winds of time and the iron will of Bayan the Patient."

label: jlama-mistral7b
name: Hollowcodex
text:
In the twilight of the age of iron, 'twas at Highstein that Kunimund, the sagacious smith, fashioned the Hollowcodex, a tome most wondrous, woven from the finest vellum. The wisdom of ages flowed through its pages, whispered secrets of old, and the fires of intuition danced within its boundaries.

In the year 506, the Hollowcodex found its first steward, none other than Kunimund the Reluctant, the shepherd of the land. He was but a humble man, yet the secrets of the Hollowcodex ignited within him a fire he had never known.

The years that followed saw the Hollowcodex passed from hand to hand, its secrets guarded by those who sought to understand the mysteries it held. It reached the hands of Trevanion, the Unquiet, a man consumed by his quest for knowledge. In his final moments, Trevanion laid the Hollowcodex to rest within his tomb, sealing its secrets for eternity.

Now, the tomb of Trevanion the Unquiet stands in the barrow of Grafell, and within it lies the Hollowcodex, its wisdom waiting for the hands of those who seek the secrets of the ages.
